# quantity uncertainty

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:quantityUncertainty`](gmeow-quantityUncertainty.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/quantityUncertainty>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/observations`](../../slices/observations.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The uncertainty (e.g. ±1 sigma) of a scalar quantity, in the same unit as the quantity value.

## Structure

**Property shape:** datatype property; [`gmeow:ScalarQuantity`](../classes/gmeow-ScalarQuantity.md) -> [`xsd:decimal`](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#decimal); functional

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:quantityUncertainty`](gmeow-quantityUncertainty.md) from [`gmeow:ScalarQuantity`](../classes/gmeow-ScalarQuantity.md) to [`xsd:decimal`](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#decimal) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to record the EPISTEMIC spread of a scalar reading — a ±1σ or tolerance figure, expressed in the same unit as [`gmeow:quantityValue`](gmeow-quantityValue.md).

### Avoid when

- Avoid conflating it with ontic determinacy ([`gmeow:hasDeterminacy`](gmeow-hasDeterminacy.md) — whether the value is crisp, vague, fuzzy) or with resolution ([`gmeow:hasGranularity`](gmeow-hasGranularity.md)); uncertainty is how-sure, an axis distinct from those ([Principle 9](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-9)).

### How to use

- State the spread in the quantity's own unit alongside [`gmeow:quantityValue`](gmeow-quantityValue.md); leave the fuzzy/probabilistic arithmetic and confidence intervals to the solver layer (P12), and carry the ontic model separately on [`gmeow:hasDeterminacy`](gmeow-hasDeterminacy.md).
